paths.description: Public entry and language-selection archetype; tested visually, on mobile, under dark/reduced-motion preferences, with performance/security/accessibility probes.
English locale homepage and destination of the primary language journey; raw HTML inspected and browser navigation attempted repeatedly.
Primary service/task-list archetype representing how residents start an Aadhaar journey.
Forms/download listing archetype representing enrolment and update paperwork.

findings.summary: The entry page ignores the user’s dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are byte-identical (51,328 bytes in the initial captures), and the DOM/CSS evidence contains no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define accessible surface/text colours with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining a light fallback.

findings.summary: Instruction text misses WCAG minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured #137eb2 text on #f2f2f2 at 4.02:1 for both English and Hindi instructions, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the blue text or lighten its background until normal text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every theme and contrast mode.

findings.summary: Language changes are abrupt document replacements with no transition or attention cue.
findings.evidence: The DOM wires every language button to document.location.replace(), contains no view-transition CSS, and the entry screenshots show no state or directional cue beyond the button grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback, and preserve/focus the destination heading after language selection.

findings.summary: Responsive behaviour is viewport-driven rather than component-driven.
findings.evidence: The captured entry CSS and static representative documents contain no @container or container-type usage; repeated cards and controls are sized through Bootstrap viewport columns.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/control regions containment and use size container queries for their internal layout, retaining viewport rules as a broad-page fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on any language button.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe found outline: none 0px and no box-shadow for all 13 buttons. Lighthouse confirms target sizes are adequate, so the failure is specifically keyboard focus visibility.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible indicator with at least a 2px contrasting outline and offset; do not remove the browser outline without an equivalent.

findings.summary: The primary language-entry journey did not complete in Chrome because the destination load never settled.
findings.evidence: Six raw-CDP attempts to load /en timed out after 120 seconds and a direct Chrome attempt timed out after 300 seconds. A later HAR of the root redirect to /hi recorded six backend image requests taking roughly 297–303 seconds and failing with ERR_TIMED_OUT; no useful recovery state appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove blocking dependency on the timing-out backend, enforce short request timeouts, render the core page shell/content independently, and expose an actionable retry/error state.

findings.summary: Resource delivery has avoidable blocking and cache inefficiency.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 430 ms potential savings from render-blocking styles and 39 KiB from missing cache lifetimes; the HAR summary also identifies uncompressed translation JS/CSS with no cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical entry styles, defer non-critical CSS, set long immutable caching for versioned assets, and compress/cache the translation bundle.

findings.summary: The entry journey ships substantial unused and duplicate client code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 98% (23 KiB) of Bootstrap CSS unused on the selector. The later application HAR transferred 2.37 MB across 88 requests, including three Google tag scripts totalling about 460 KiB and 39 script requests overall.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace full Bootstrap on the selector with scoped critical CSS, load one analytics configuration, and split/defer application code by route and user intent.

findings.summary: The entry surface lacks semantic page structure and visible keyboard orientation.
findings.evidence: The rendered entry has no h1–h6, header, nav, main or footer landmark, and the only named role is a generic group labelled “Basic example”; all focused controls have no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a main landmark and a real h1 for the language prompt, give the group a descriptive label, and provide a persistent :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and the error template is not a sound HTML document.
findings.evidence: Both entry images omit width and height; Lighthouse fails unsized-images. The representative raw pages contain many more dimensionless images, while the 404 response has no doctype, html lang, title, viewport or h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add numeric intrinsic width/height to every img and serve the 404 through the normal document template with doctype, language, metadata, landmarks and an h1.

findings.summary: The entry page logs a failed favicon request.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a 404 console/network error for /en/uidai-website/templates/tjbase/favicon.ico.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the favicon URL and verify the asset returns 200 on every locale route.

findings.summary: Metadata is incomplete and insufficiently unique across representative pages.
findings.evidence: The language selector has no meta description. Four English archetypes use distinct titles but the same generic UIDAI description, and none exposes a canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the selector and each template a concise page-specific description and emit a self-referencing canonical URL.

findings.summary: Crawler discovery and indexing signals are internally inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Requests to /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml returned styled 404/error HTML rather than valid directives/XML; representative pages expose no canonical or hreflang links, and the search HTML includes three anchors without href.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid robots.txt and XML sitemap files, add self-canonicals plus locale hreflang alternates, and ensure navigational links have real href values.

findings.summary: Public organization and service pages lack structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The four raw English archetypes include Open Graph tags but zero application/ld+json blocks despite representing a government organization, services and forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for GovernmentOrganization/WebSite and relevant service or article entities, matching the visible page content.

findings.summary: The exact entry response omits browser security headers even though the newer locale response supplies them.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer or permissions policy on the language selector. A separate curl response for /en did include these controls, showing inconsistent policy by template.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the same CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy at the edge to every response, including selector and error templates.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics and translation traffic is disproportionate on initial entry.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 31 third-party requests and 627,109 transferred bytes, including three Google tag scripts and repeated translation calls that returned 401.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics to one consent-aware endpoint, delay it until needed/allowed, self-host or trim translation assets, and prevent unauthorized retry traffic.

findings.summary: The multilingual selector does not mark per-language direction and uses no logical layout properties.
findings.evidence: The page html language is en, but all 13 language labels, including RTL Urdu, are rendered without dir attributes. Static summaries found physical CSS and no logical-property evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang and dir on each language label (dir=rtl for Urdu) and migrate reusable spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: Media and third-party cost is excessive for a government service gateway.
findings.evidence: The application HAR transfers 2.37 MB: a 440 KiB chatbot GIF, 444 KiB of decorative background WebP images, 627 KiB of third-party resources and duplicated analytics. Six backend media requests ran for about five minutes before timeout.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the GIF with a small static/modern animation, remove or sharply compress decorative backgrounds, consolidate analytics, lazy-load optional tools and cancel timed-out media requests quickly.

taskList.title: Make locale entry and backend-dependent content load reliably
Restore visible keyboard focus and semantic page structure
Apply security headers consistently to every template
Reduce, defer and deduplicate scripts, media and third parties
Repair crawler infrastructure and indexing metadata
Meet text contrast and user colour preferences
Add intrinsic media dimensions and repair error/favicon assets
Make multilingual layout direction-aware and interaction transitions clear
